about_the_game:
In Liberty Dogs, you play as one of six young rebels rising up against the dictatorship of Santo Calvario, a fictional Caribbean island in the 1980s. Armed with your mask and your courage, you’ll battle soldiers, criminals, and local kingpins to free your people.

This game was developed entirely by me, a solo indie developer, as my final degree project. It represents my very first complete videogame, built from scratch as a labor of passion. Liberty Dogs is currently in its earliest beta/alpha stage, which means there are still bugs, rough edges, and mechanics to polish — but it’s fully playable and already captures the vision I had in mind.

The project was designed to be enjoyed both with keyboard/mouse and full controller support, ensuring smooth combat and movement no matter how you prefer to play. At its heart, Liberty Dogs tells an original story, inspired by comics and animation, where freedom, morality, and rebellion collide.

Key Features:

  • Third-person action: Fluid combat combining melee, shooting, and explosives.

  • Honor system: Your decisions shape the revolution. Will you save lives or spread chaos?

  • Varied missions: Rescue victims, gather supplies, chase criminals, or sabotage the regime’s monuments.

  • Semi-open world: Explore diverse levels filled with enemies, puzzles, objects, and secrets.

  • Customization: Personalize your hero and upgrade with coins and rewards.

  • Original cutscenes: Story-driven moments created entirely by a solo indie developer.

This is the very first step of Liberty Dogs: a raw but passionate indie game, developed solo and born as a graduation project. Will you become the hero Santo Calvario desperately needs… or the villain it fears?

short_description: Liberty Dogs is a third-person action-adventure game set in the 1980s on a fictional Caribbean island under dictatorship. Join a group of masked heroes and fight against soldiers, cartels, and criminals while forging your own path. Complete main, side missions and customize your character.
